newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sasol says confident of Brazil exports.
newsitem.headline: Sasol says confident of Brazil exports.

text.p: Synthetic fuel producer Sasol Ltd said on Friday complying with new Brazilian specifications for motor fuel alcohol would have little effect on the company's export earnings.
"There will be a slight (negative) adjustment. It will be negligible," Sasol spokesman Alfonso Niemand said.
South Africa's Financial Mail magazine reported Sasol faced earnings losses of more than US$75 million this year as a result of Brazil's decision to slash fuel alcohol imports by over 50 percent.
The Brazilian government has said its priority is to produce enough alcohol from its 1997/98 sugar crop to eliminate the need for imports.
Sasol's Niemand declined to comment on possible import cuts.
He said the new specifications had prompted Sasol to renegotiate certain terms of its 400 million rand (US$90 million)-a-year motor fuel alcohol export contract with Brazil.
"We are reformulating our product specifications and believe that the bulk of our motor fuel alcohol production will continue to be placed in the Brazilian market on a long term basis," Niemand said.
He declined to give pricing details for Sasol's reformulated fuel alcohol product.
Sasol has been exporting motor fuel alcohol to Brazil for three years.

Niemand said previous markets for the product, including worldwide chemical markets and some European and South African motor fuel markets, remained open to Sasol but the Brazilian market was likely to yield the best long term returns.
